a: ab, ā (prep. + abl.) — from, away from; by (ā before consonants)

an: an (conj.) — or, or rather; introduces the second part of a question

ante: ante (prep. + acc., adv.) — before, in front of; previously

arma: arma, -ōrum (n. pl.) — arms, weapons; war (acc./nom. pl.)

ast: ast (conj.) — but (archaic, solemn form of at)
atria: ātrium, -ī (n.) — hall, court of a house (acc. pl.)

ceu: ceu (adv., conj.) — as, like, just as

cum: cum — (conj.) when, since, although; (prep. + abl.) with

danaum: Danaī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Danaans, the Greeks (gen. pl., old form = Danaōrum)

dedit: dō, dare, dedī, datum — to give; to grant (+ inf.) (3rd sg. perf.)

domus: domus, -ūs (f.) — house, home, dwelling (nom. sg.) · gen. sg. (of the house; domus scelus)
dum: dum (conj.) — while; until (+ subj., of a goal looked forward to)
dura: dūrus, -a, -um — hard, harsh (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
dymasque: Dymās, -antis (m.) — Dymas, Trojan companion of Aeneas (nom. sg.) + -que 'and'

erat: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd sg. impf.)
et: et — and; also, even; et… et: both… and
eurus: Eurus, -ī (m.) — Eurus, the east (south-east) wind (nom. sg.)

ferre: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — to carry, bring (pres. inf.)

fuissent: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3 pl. pluperf. subj.; with defensa, pluperf. pass.)
fuit: sum, esse, fuī — to be; there was (3rd sg. perf.)
gemini: geminus, -a, -um — twin, double, a pair (m. nom. pl.)
genus: genus, generis (n.) — race, family, birth, kind (nom./acc. sg.)
hanc: hic, haec, hoc — this (f. acc. sg.)

hoc: hic, haec, hoc — this (n. nom./acc. sg.; m./n. abl. sg.)

iam: iam (adv.) — now, already; iam… iam, now… now
illi: ille, illa, illud — that; illī, they, those (m. nom. pl.); to him/her (dat. sg.)
imo: īmus, -a, -um — lowest, deepest, innermost (n./m. abl. sg.; superl. of īnferus)

insidiis: īnsidiae, -ārum (f. pl.) — ambush, treachery, wiles (abl. pl.)

ipsi: ipse, ipsa, ipsum — himself, themselves, the very (m. nom. pl.; dat. sg.)
ipsos: ipse, ipsa, ipsum — himself, herself, itself; the very (m. acc. pl.)
ipsum: ipse, ipsa, ipsum — himself, herself, itself; the very (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
iter: iter, itineris (n.) — journey, way, course (acc./nom. sg.)

laetus: laetus, -a, -um — glad, joyful, proud (m. nom. sg.)
lapsa: lābor, lābī, lapsus sum (dep.) — to glide, slip, fall (perf. part., f. nom. sg.)
limina: līmen, līminis (n.) — threshold, doorway, house (nom./acc. pl.)

manebant: maneō, -ēre, mānsī, mānsum — to remain, stay, abide (3rd pl. impf.)
mecum: mē + cum — with me (cum enclitic after the pronoun)

micat: micō, micāre, micuī — to flash, flicker, gleam (3rd sg. pres.)

navis: nāvis, -is (f.) — ship (acc. pl., = nāvēs; also nom./gen. sg.)
nec: nec, neque — and not, nor; nec… nec, neither… nor

notusque: Notus, -ī (m.) — Notus, the south wind (nom. sg.) + -que 'and'
novus: novus, -a, -um — new, fresh, strange (m. nom. sg.)
numine: nūmen, nūminis (n.) — divine will, divinity, godhead (abl. sg.)

pars: pars, partis (f.) — part, share, portion (nom. sg.)

pectore: pectus, pectoris (n.) — breast, chest; heart (abl. sg.)

quisque: quisque, quaeque, quidque — each one, everyone (m. nom. sg.)
quondam: quondam (adv.) — once, formerly, at one time

quos: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel. or interrog., m. acc. pl.)

regis: regō, regere, rēxī, rēctum — to rule, direct (2nd sg. pres.)
relicti: relinquō, -ere, -līquī, -lictum — to leave behind, abandon (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl.; gen. sg.)

se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
sedes: sēdēs, sēdis (f.) — seat, abode, settlement (acc./nom. pl.)

sese: sē, sēsē — emphatic reflexive, himself, itself, themselves (acc.)
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way

tendens: tendō, tendere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, stretch out (pres. part., nom. sg.)

unus: ūnus, -a, -um — one, alone, a single (m. nom. sg.)

vadimus: vādō, -ere — to go, advance, rush (1 pl. pres.)
venti: ventus, -ī (m.) — wind (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl., in address (sine nūmine, ventī)
